description: An introduction to electronic mail and other forms of electronic communication, covering email addresses, composing and managing messages, attachments, netiquette, and the advantages and risks of digital communication tools.

mcq.questionText: What does the word 'email' stand for?
mcq.explanation: Email is short for electronic mail, which is the exchange of messages between people using electronic devices over a network.

mcq.questionText: In the email address learner@school.co.tz, which part is the username?
mcq.explanation: The username is the part before the @ symbol that identifies the specific account holder.

mcq.questionText: Which symbol always separates the username from the domain name in every email address?
mcq.explanation: The @ (at) symbol is a required part of every email address and separates the username from the domain.

mcq.questionText: Which field would you use to send a copy of an email to someone while letting all recipients see that this person also received it?
mcq.explanation: CC (Carbon Copy) sends a visible copy to additional recipients, and everyone can see who was copied.

mcq.questionText: What is the main purpose of the BCC field in an email?

options.text: To send a copy without other recipients seeing that address
To set the subject of the message
To reply to all recipients automatically

mcq.explanation: BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) sends a hidden copy so other recipients cannot see that address, protecting privacy.

mcq.questionText: Which feature lets you send an email you received on to a third person who was not an original recipient?
mcq.explanation: Forwarding passes a received message on to a new recipient, usually keeping the original content.

options.text: The subject line of the message
A file sent along with the email message
The signature at the end of an email

mcq.explanation: An attachment is a separate file, such as a document or picture, that is sent together with an email message.

options.text: The speed of an internet connection
The rules for polite and proper behaviour online

mcq.explanation: Netiquette is a combination of 'network' and 'etiquette' and refers to good manners when communicating online.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an instant messaging activity?

options.text: Sending a real-time text chat message to a friend
Saving a document to a flash disk

mcq.explanation: Instant messaging allows two or more people to exchange typed messages in real time over a network.

mcq.questionText: Which electronic communication tool allows people in different locations to see and hear each other live?
mcq.explanation: Video conferencing uses cameras and microphones to let people in different places hold a live audio and video meeting.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is a clear advantage of email over traditional postal mail?
mcq.explanation: Email is delivered in seconds or minutes, while postal mail can take days, making email much faster.

mcq.questionText: Unwanted and unsolicited bulk email is commonly called what?
mcq.explanation: Spam is junk email sent in bulk to many people who did not ask for it, often containing adverts or scams.

mcq.questionText: Which part of an email tells the recipient what the message is about before they open it?
mcq.explanation: The subject line is a short summary of the email's topic and helps the reader know what the message concerns.

mcq.questionText: A trick where an email pretends to be from a trusted organisation to steal your password is known as what?
mcq.explanation: Phishing is a scam where fake emails imitate trusted sources to trick people into revealing passwords or personal details.

mcq.questionText: When you click 'Reply All' on an email sent to many people, what happens?

options.text: Your response goes only to the original sender
Your response goes to the sender and all other recipients
The original email is permanently deleted
The message is saved as a draft without sending

mcq.explanation: Reply All sends your message to the original sender and everyone who received the original email, so it should be used carefully.

fib.questionText: The part of an email address that comes after the @ symbol is called the _____ name.
fib.explanation: The domain name identifies the mail server or organisation that hosts the email account, for example gmail.com.

fib.questionText: Sending a hidden copy of an email so that other recipients cannot see that address uses the _____ field.
fib.explanation: BCC stands for Blind Carbon Copy and keeps the listed addresses hidden from the other recipients.

fib.questionText: A file such as a photo or document sent together with an email is known as an _____.
fib.explanation: An attachment is an extra file added to an email so the recipient can download and open it.

fib.questionText: The set of polite rules for behaving well when communicating online is called _____.
fib.explanation: Netiquette combines 'network' and 'etiquette' and guides courteous online communication.

fib.questionText: Unwanted bulk junk email sent to many people is called _____.
fib.explanation: Spam clutters inboxes and may contain adverts, scams, or harmful links.

fib.questionText: Replying to a message and sending it on to a new person who was not an original recipient is called _____.
fib.explanation: Forwarding passes a received email on to another person, usually keeping the original message.

fib.questionText: The folder where newly received emails first arrive is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The inbox stores incoming messages until the user reads, replies to, or deletes them.

fib.questionText: A short line summarising what an email is about is called the _____ line.
fib.explanation: The subject line helps the recipient quickly understand the purpose of the email.

fib.questionText: A communication tool that lets people in different places see and hear each other live using cameras and microphones is called _____ conferencing.
fib.explanation: Video conferencing supports live meetings with both picture and sound over the internet.

fib.questionText: A scam email that pretends to be from a trusted source in order to steal personal information is an example of _____.
fib.explanation: Phishing tricks users into giving away passwords or bank details by imitating real organisations.

tf.questionText: An email address must contain the @ symbol.
tf.explanation: Every valid email address uses the @ symbol to separate the username from the domain name.

tf.questionText: When you use the BCC field, the other recipients can see all the BCC addresses.
tf.explanation: BCC addresses are hidden, so other recipients cannot see who was placed in the BCC field.

tf.questionText: Email messages can be sent and received at any time of the day or night.
tf.explanation: Email works around the clock, and messages wait in the inbox until the recipient is ready to read them.

tf.questionText: It is good netiquette to type an entire email message in capital letters.
tf.explanation: Writing in all capitals is seen as SHOUTING and is considered rude, so it should be avoided.

tf.questionText: You should open attachments from unknown senders without checking, because they are always safe.
tf.explanation: Attachments from unknown senders may carry viruses or malware, so they should not be opened carelessly.

tf.questionText: Instant messaging usually allows people to exchange messages in real time.
tf.explanation: Instant messaging delivers typed messages almost immediately, enabling live conversations.

tf.questionText: Email completely removes all risks to privacy and security.
tf.explanation: Email still carries risks such as spam, phishing, viruses, and accounts being hacked.

tf.questionText: The same email can be sent to several recipients at once.
tf.explanation: By listing multiple addresses in the To, CC, or BCC fields, one email can reach many people at the same time.

tf.questionText: Social media platforms are an example of electronic communication tools.
tf.explanation: Social media lets people share messages, photos, and updates electronically with others online.

tf.questionText: Forwarding an email creates a brand new message with no connection to the original content.
tf.explanation: Forwarding normally keeps the original message and passes it on to a new recipient.

summary.correctAnswer: Email is electronic mail used to send and receive messages over a network.
summary.explanation: It allows fast exchange of text and files between users with email accounts.

summary.correctAnswer: Username, the @ symbol, and the domain name.
summary.explanation: For example, in name@example.com, 'name' is the username and 'example.com' is the domain.

summary.correctAnswer: CC sends a visible copy of an email to additional recipients.
summary.explanation: Everyone can see who was copied in the CC field.

summary.correctAnswer: BCC sends a hidden copy so other recipients cannot see that address.
summary.explanation: It protects the privacy of the copied recipients.

summary.correctAnswer: An attachment is a file sent along with an email message.
summary.explanation: Documents, images, and other files can be attached and downloaded by the recipient.

summary.correctAnswer: Netiquette is the set of polite rules for communicating online.
summary.explanation: It includes being respectful, clear, and avoiding shouting in capital letters.

summary.correctAnswer: Replying answers the sender, while forwarding passes the message to a new person.
summary.explanation: Reply responds to the original sender; forward sends the email on to someone else.

summary.correctAnswer: Email, instant messaging, video conferencing, and social media.
summary.explanation: These tools let people communicate electronically over networks.

summary.correctAnswer: It is fast, cheap, and can reach many people anywhere at once.
summary.explanation: Messages and files are delivered quickly across distances at low cost.

summary.correctAnswer: Spam, phishing, viruses, and loss of privacy.
summary.explanation: Users must be careful with unknown messages and protect their personal information.

hoq.questionText: A teacher wants to email exam results to 40 parents individually so that no parent can see the email addresses of the other parents. Which approach is best?

options.text: Put all 40 addresses in the To field
Put all 40 addresses in the CC field
Put all 40 addresses in the BCC field
Forward the email 40 separate times to each parent

hoq.explanation: Using BCC hides every address from the others, protecting each parent's privacy while still sending one message.

hoq.questionText: A student receives an email claiming to be from their bank, asking them to click a link and confirm their password urgently. What is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Click the link quickly and enter the password before the deadline
Treat it as possible phishing and do not click or share the password
Forward it to all friends so they can also confirm their passwords
Reply with the password to prove the account is active

hoq.explanation: Urgent requests for passwords through links are a common phishing tactic, so the student should not click or reveal any details.

hoq.questionText: A company needs to hold a meeting where staff in three different cities can see and hear each other and share their screens at the same time. Which tool is most suitable?

options.text: Posting a letter to each office
Saving notes on a shared flash disk

hoq.explanation: Video conferencing supports live audio, video, and screen sharing among people in different locations simultaneously.
